description: REAL turbo-rails signed stream names, produced by the dummy Rails application (gem/test/dummy) through Turbo::StreamsChannel.signed_stream_name. Format: base64_standard(JSON(stream_string)) + "--" + hex(HMAC-SHA256(key, encoded)). The key is raw bytes exported as strict base64 in input.key_base64; Rust must decode it to bytes (ORBITCAST_TURBO_SECRET_BASE64), never treat it as text. `rust_status` records whether src/streams.rs MessageVerifier accepts the case as-is.

producer.key_source: Rails.application.key_generator.generate_key("turbo/signed_stream_verifier_key") in a real application; pinned raw bytes here

rust_contract.key: base64-decode input.key_base64 to raw bytes; key it into SecretBytes/MessageVerifier
rust_contract.controller: StreamsController::new(StreamsConfig { turbo: true, turbo_secret: Some(key), .. }, namespace) .handles(input.identifier) is true and .resolve(input.identifier) yields StreamResult { stream: expect.stream, whisper: false, presence: false }
rust_contract.negative: flipping one hex character of expect.signature must yield VerifyError::InvalidSignature; verifying with a different key must not fall back to the Orbitcast claims secret
rust_contract.mismatch_rule: a case with "rust_status": "mismatch" documents real turbo-rails output the current verifier does NOT accept; assert the documented rejection, do not silently loosen the verifier

cases.name: turbo_stream_from_demo
cases.description: Exactly what `turbo_stream_from "demo"` puts in the page: Turbo::StreamsChannel.signed_stream_name(["demo"]).

cases.name: plain_string_streamable
cases.description: The single-string form, signed_stream_name("demo"). Turbo joins arrays with ':' but a bare string is passed through, so this must equal the one-element array case.

cases.name: joined_streamables_padded_base64
cases.description: Multiple streamables are joined with ':'. The payload length forces base64 '=' padding, which a URL-safe/unpadded decoder would reject — Rust decodes with the padded standard alphabet.

cases.name: unicode_streamable
cases.description: Non-ASCII stream name. turbo-rails' JSON serializer emits raw UTF-8 (no \u escapes); Rust decodes base64 -> UTF-8 -> JSON string.

cases.name: quote_and_backslash_streamable
cases.description: Stream name containing characters the JSON serializer must escape. The escaped bytes are what the HMAC covers.
